sentences.en: There was a time when most detective stories
sentences.zh: 曾几何时，大多数侦探故事

sentences.en: featured the brilliant insights of a genius.
sentences.zh: 都以天才的敏锐洞察力为卖点。

sentences.en: Sherlock Holmes and Miss Marple noticed clues the rest of us didn't
sentences.zh: 夏洛克·福尔摩斯和马普尔小姐能注意到我们常人忽略的线索，

sentences.en: and solved mysteries using little more than their eyes and their intuition.
sentences.zh: 并仅凭双眼和直觉就能破解谜团。

sentences.en: In the story The Adventure of the Blue Carbuncle,
sentences.zh: 在《蓝宝石探案》的故事中，

sentences.en: Sherlock Holmes inspects a hat that was found next to a stolen gem.
sentences.zh: 夏洛克·福尔摩斯检查了一顶在被盗宝石旁发现的帽子。

sentences.en: He tells his friend John Watson that the hat's owner
sentences.zh: 他告诉朋友约翰·华生，这顶帽子的主人

sentences.en: is a smart, formerly wealthy man who recently turned evil.
sentences.zh: 是一位聪明、曾经富有但最近变坏了的男人。

sentences.en: He is middle-aged, out of shape, recently cut his hair,
sentences.zh: 他已届中年，身材走样，最近刚剪了头发，

sentences.en: and his wife no longer loves him.
sentences.zh: 而且他的妻子不再爱他了。

sentences.en: All of this from simply looking at the hat.
sentences.zh: 这一切仅仅通过观察那顶帽子就能得出。

sentences.en: In the real world, crime solving today relies less on sharp eyes and intuitive leaps
sentences.zh: 在现实世界中，如今的犯罪侦破不再那么依赖敏锐的观察和直觉的飞跃，

sentences.en: and more on the science of forensics.
sentences.zh: 而更多地依赖法医科学。

sentences.en: Suspects leave fingerprints at scenes of crime
sentences.zh: 嫌疑人在犯罪现场留下指纹，

sentences.en: and tiny strands of DNA can identify one person out of billions.
sentences.zh: 微量的 DNA 就能从数十亿人中锁定某一个人。

sentences.en: In recent years, psychologists have gotten into the game.
sentences.zh: 近年来，心理学家也加入了这场博弈。

sentences.en: They have discovered another set of clues
sentences.zh: 他们发现了另一套线索，

sentences.en: that can give us a window into a suspect's mind.
sentences.zh: 可以让我们窥探嫌疑人的内心世界。

sentences.en: The source of this hidden information?
sentences.zh: 这些隐藏信息的来源是什么？

sentences.en: The words we use in both speech and writing reveal a lot about us.
sentences.zh: 我们在口语和书面语中使用的词汇揭示了关于我们的许多信息。

sentences.en: They can give us insight into a potential criminal, yes,
sentences.zh: 它们不仅能让我们洞察潜在的罪犯，

sentences.en: but also whether someone is depressed,
sentences.zh: 还能揭示某人是否抑郁，

sentences.en: even how long a lover will remain in a romantic relationship.
sentences.zh: 甚至能预测一段恋情还能维持多久。

sentences.en: What your pronouns and prepositions really say about you.
sentences.zh: 你的代词和介词真正说明了什么。

sentences.en: Have you ever gotten a confusing message from a friend or family member?
sentences.zh: 你是否曾收到过朋友或家人发来的令人困惑的信息？
也许是一条短信或一封邮件。

sentences.en: I have no idea what this person is actually feeling.
sentences.zh: 我根本不知道这个人到底是什么感受。

sentences.en: If only there was a way to decipher what she really means.
sentences.zh: 如果有一种方法能解读出他真正的意思就好了。

sentences.en: In recent years, scientists have tried to do exactly that.
sentences.zh: 近年来，科学家们正是试图做到这一点。

sentences.en: They find that if we pay close attention to the patterns in speech and writing,
sentences.zh: 他们发现，如果我们密切关注言语和写作中的模式，

sentences.en: we can understand profound things about others and even ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我们就能理解关于他人甚至我们自己的深刻道理。

sentences.en: At the University of Texas at Austin,
sentences.zh: 在德克萨斯大学奥斯汀分校，

sentences.en: psychologist James Pennebaker has spent decades studying how the words we use
sentences.zh: 心理学家詹姆斯·彭尼贝克花了数十年时间研究我们使用的词汇

sentences.en: can be an X-ray into our minds.
sentences.zh: 如何成为我们思想的 X 光片。

sentences.en: Jamie Pennebaker, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 杰米·彭尼贝克，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Jamie, early on in your career,
sentences.zh: 杰米，在你的职业生涯早期，

sentences.en: you were studying how writing can help people get over traumatic experiences.
sentences.zh: 你曾研究写作如何帮助人们克服创伤经历。

sentences.en: But as part of that research, you noticed something.
sentences.zh: 但在那项研究中，你注意到了一些事情。

sentences.en: The language people use changed as their mental states changed.
sentences.zh: 人们使用的语言会随着心理状态的变化而改变。

sentences.en: Can you tell me how this discovery unfolded?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我这个发现是如何展开的吗？

sentences.en: I was trying to figure out why is it that writing about an upsetting experience
sentences.zh: 我当时试图弄清楚，为什么书写痛苦的经历

sentences.en: And it occurred to me I needed a more objective way to look at essays.
sentences.zh: 我意识到我需要一种更客观的方法来审视这些文章。

sentences.en: And so I looked for a computer program to analyze the text.
sentences.zh: 于是我找了一个计算机程序来分析文本。

sentences.en: And I ended up asking one of my graduate students
sentences.zh: 最后我请我的一位研究生

sentences.en: to help put together a computer program that could analyze language.
sentences.zh: 帮忙编写了一个可以分析语言的计算机程序。

sentences.en: And it was that program that allowed us to all of a sudden
sentences.zh: 正是那个程序让我们突然之间

sentences.en: start to see writing samples in ways that I had never imagined we'd be able to do.
sentences.zh: 开始以我从未想象过的方式审视写作样本。

sentences.en: The computer program that Jamie developed could analyze a text,
sentences.zh: 杰米开发的计算机程序可以分析文本，

sentences.en: breaking it down by word choice, parts of speech, and meaning.
sentences.zh: 通过词汇选择、词性分析和语义来对其进行拆解。

sentences.en: it was a dark and stormy night.
sentences.zh: 那是一个黑暗而暴风雨的夜晚。

sentences.en: The program would categorize the word it as a pronoun.
sentences.zh: 程序会将“it”这个词归类为代词。

sentences.en: The word was would be counted as a verb.

sentences.zh: 暴风雨的是一个形容词。

sentences.en: Jamie then brought volunteers into the lab
sentences.zh: 杰米把志愿者带进实验室，

sentences.en: and asked them to give him writing samples.
He analyzed their writing through the computer program
sentences.zh: 他通过计算机程序分析了他们的写作，

sentences.en: and then compared the results to the personalities of the writers.
sentences.zh: 然后将结果与作者的个性进行了对比。

sentences.en: He came to several astonishing conclusions.
sentences.zh: 他得出了几个惊人的结论。

sentences.en: One of the first was that men and women employ language differently.
sentences.zh: 其中第一个结论是，男性和女性使用语言的方式不同。

sentences.en: Jamie assumed that men are more likely than women to act in boastful ways.
sentences.zh: 杰米认为男性比女性更有可能表现得自吹自擂。

sentences.en: So he expected they would refer a lot to themselves.
sentences.zh: 所以他预计他们会大量提及自己。

sentences.en: They would use a lot of words like I.
sentences.zh: 他们会使用很多像“我”这样的词。

sentences.en: Jamie figured women would use words like we.
sentences.zh: 杰米推测女性会使用像“我们”这样的词。

sentences.en: The most striking early discovery was that looking at men and women,
sentences.zh: 早期最惊人的发现是，观察男性和女性时，

sentences.en: they used language in ways that made no sense to me.
sentences.zh: 他们使用语言的方式让我感到莫名其妙。

sentences.en: I found that women used I words, I, me and my, at much higher rates than men.
sentences.zh: 我发现女性使用“我”类词汇，即“我”、“我（宾格）”和“我的”，频率远高于男性。

sentences.en: I expected big differences in the use of we.
sentences.zh: 我原本预计在“我们”的使用上会有巨大差异。

sentences.en: But in fact, men and women used we words at the same rates.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，男性和女性使用“我们”类词汇的频率是一样的。

sentences.en: And there were these other parts of speech that were just very different,
sentences.zh: 还有其他一些词性差异非常大，

sentences.en: and I had no idea what they meant.
sentences.zh: 我完全不知道它们意味着什么。

sentences.en: And over the years, we did more and more studies,
sentences.zh: 多年来，我们做了越来越多的研究，

sentences.en: and part of it was men and women are paying attention to the world differently.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是男性和女性关注世界的方式不同。

sentences.en: Women are looking and are more interested in other human beings.
sentences.zh: 女性更关注也更感兴趣于其他人。

sentences.en: And by definition, if you're interested in human beings, you have to use pronouns.
sentences.zh: 根据定义，如果你对人感兴趣，你就必须使用代词。

sentences.en: Words like he, she, they, we, I, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 像“他”、“她”、“他们”、“我们”、“我”等等这样的词。

sentences.en: And if you're interested in objects and things, which men tend to be, you use nouns and articles.
sentences.zh: 而如果你对物体和事物感兴趣，男性往往如此，你就会使用名词和冠词。

sentences.en: And so all of a sudden, I realized the world was way more complex than I ever thought.
sentences.zh: 所以突然之间，我意识到世界比我曾经想象的要复杂得多。

sentences.en: I confess I was skeptical about these conclusions.
sentences.zh: 我承认，我曾对这些结论持怀疑态度。

sentences.en: There are all kinds of pop psychology claims about gender differences that mostly rely on stereotypes about men and women.
sentences.zh: 关于性别差异的流行心理学说法五花八门，大多依赖于对男女的刻板印象。

sentences.en: But then Jamie told me about another dimension of this research.
sentences.zh: 但随后杰米告诉了我这项研究的另一个维度。

sentences.en: It had an experimental quality to it.
It tracked individuals getting supplements of testosterone, the primary male sex hormone.
sentences.zh: 它追踪了接受睾酮（主要的男性性激素）补充剂的个体。

sentences.en: Testosterone seems to affect the way we see our worlds.
sentences.zh: 睾酮似乎影响了我们看待世界的方式。

sentences.en: And several years ago, working with Jim Dabbs and others who had been doing work on testosterone,
sentences.zh: 几年前，与吉姆·达布斯及其他一直在研究睾酮的人合作时，

sentences.en: we were able to study a person who was transitioning from female to male and was taking periodic injections of testosterone.
sentences.zh: 我们得以研究了一位正在从女性向男性过渡并定期注射睾酮的人。

sentences.en: I was studying this person's diaries over time and trying to find out when this person took the testosterone injections, did their language change?
sentences.zh: 我长期研究这个人的日记，试图找出当他注射睾酮时，他的语言是否发生了变化？

sentences.en: I was telling a friend of this, and this friend was an academic, and he was saying,
sentences.zh: 我把这件事告诉了一位朋友，他是一位学者，他说，

sentences.en: wow, that's weird, I've been taking testosterone as well, because he had moved to a farm and he was older by this time,
sentences.zh: 哇，这太奇怪了，我也一直在服用睾酮，因为他搬到了农场，而且当时年纪大了，

sentences.en: and he started taking testosterone to increase his upper body strength.
sentences.zh: 他开始服用睾酮来增加上半身力量。

sentences.en: And I asked him, would he mind sharing when he had taken these shots, and also sharing his outgoing emails for the previous year.
sentences.zh: 我问他是否介意分享他注射的时间，以及分享他过去一年的外发邮件。

sentences.en: So for both of them, I could look at when they took shots, which was usually about once every three weeks,
sentences.zh: 所以对于他们两人，我都可以观察他们注射的时间，通常大约每三周一次，

sentences.en: and how their language changed from before taking the testosterone to the three weeks afterwards.
sentences.zh: 以及他们的语言从注射前到注射后三周内发生了怎样的变化。

sentences.en: And I found the same kind of changes.
And it was not what either of them expected at all.
sentences.zh: 而且这完全出乎他们两人的意料。

sentences.en: And that was, when the individuals took the testosterone shots, they started using pronouns, he, she, they, etc., at lower rates.
sentences.zh: 那就是，当个体注射睾酮后，他们开始减少使用代词，如“他”、“她”、“他们”等。

sentences.en: It's almost as though they became less interested in other human beings.
sentences.zh: 这几乎就像他们对其他人变得不那么感兴趣了。

sentences.en: Testosterone then didn't make people talk more about power or aggression or anger or anxiety or anything.
sentences.zh: 所以睾酮并没有让人更多地谈论权力、攻击性、愤怒、焦虑或任何其他东西。

sentences.en: There were no differences there, only this lack of interest in humans after taking a testosterone shot.
sentences.zh: 这方面没有任何差异，只有在注射睾酮后对人类缺乏兴趣这一点。

sentences.en: Jamie had discovered that the language people use reveals something about what is happening inside their heads.
sentences.zh: 杰米发现，人们使用的语言揭示了他们大脑内部正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: Words reflect not just what we are trying to communicate, but how we see the world, how we see each other.
sentences.zh: 词汇不仅反映了我们试图交流的内容，还反映了我们如何看待世界，如何看待彼此。

sentences.en: Fascinated, Jamie started using his language analysis tool to study other facets of human behavior.
sentences.zh: 杰米对此着迷，开始使用他的语言分析工具来研究人类行为的其他方面。

sentences.en: He quickly noticed a group of words that was extremely important, but these are not words most people would think are important.
sentences.zh: 他很快注意到一组极其重要的词汇，但这些词并不是大多数人认为重要的词。

sentences.en: I focus a lot on a group of words called function words.
sentences.zh: 我非常关注一组被称为功能词的词汇。

sentences.en: These are the words you learned in high school.
sentences.zh: 这些是你高中时学过的词。

sentences.en: They're the most boring words in language.
sentences.zh: 它们是语言中最枯燥的词。

sentences.en: To, of, for, for, auxiliary verbs, am, is.
sentences.zh: 到，的，为了，为了，助动词，是，是。

sentences.en: All of these are words that don't have any solid meaning like a noun does or a verb or adjective does.
sentences.zh: 所有这些词不像名词、动词或形容词那样具有具体的含义。

sentences.en: What I started to discover was it was these function words, which are telling us how people are seeing the world,
sentences.zh: 我开始发现，正是这些功能词告诉我们人们是如何看待世界的，

sentences.en: how they're negotiating with others, how they're thinking about themselves and others.
sentences.zh: 他们如何与他人互动，以及他们如何思考自己和他人。

sentences.en: And with this, we can start to get a picture of their personality, if you like.
sentences.zh: 通过这些，我们就可以开始勾勒出他们的性格轮廓了，如果你愿意的话。

sentences.en: So, for example, I could go out to your listening audience, ask them to send me their, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，我可以去联系你们的听众，请他们发给我，你知道的，

sentences.en: their last two or three emails that they sent out.
sentences.zh: 他们最近发出的两三封邮件。

sentences.en: And people who use a high number of pronouns like he, she, they, you, et cetera,
sentences.zh: 而那些大量使用代词的人，比如“他”、“她”、“他们”、“你”等等，

sentences.en: those people are more socially connected.
sentences.zh: 这些人通常社交联系更紧密。

sentences.en: They're more interested in other human beings.
She is one of those people who will maintain composure in the situation.
sentences.zh: 她就是那种在任何情况下都能保持冷静的人。

sentences.en: I can't believe he did that.
sentences.zh: 我真不敢相信他竟然做了那种事。

sentences.en: Or another interesting one is people who are anxious.
sentences.zh: 或者另一个有趣的例子是那些感到焦虑的人。

sentences.en: Now, a person who's anxious will use anxiety-related words, words like worry, upset, nervous.
sentences.zh: 一个焦虑的人会使用与焦虑相关的词汇，比如“担心”、“不安”、“紧张”。

sentences.en: But they're also very much self-focused.
sentences.zh: 但他们也非常关注自我。

sentences.en: And they tend to use pronouns like I, I, me, and my, I refer to as I words.
sentences.zh: 他们倾向于使用像“我”、“我”、“我”、“我的”这类代词，我称之为“我”字词。

sentences.en: At much higher rate than people who are not anxious.
sentences.zh: 使用频率远高于那些不焦虑的人。

sentences.en: And in fact, all of us, when we're anxious, we start using more I words.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们所有人，当我们焦虑时，都会开始更多地使用“我”字词。

sentences.en: And the same thing is true of depression.
Any emotion that makes us look inward, we will start using I words more.
sentences.zh: 任何让我们向内审视的情绪，都会促使我们更多地使用“我”字词。

sentences.en: And even if we're physically sick or in pain, we use I words more.
sentences.zh: 甚至当我们身体不适或感到疼痛时，我们也会更多地使用“我”字词。

sentences.en: In other words, I words are reflecting self-focus.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，“我”字词反映了对自我的关注。

sentences.en: I mean, what's striking here, Jamie, is that I think when most people think about language,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，杰米，这里令人震惊的是，我认为当大多数人思考语言时，

sentences.en: they think about words that have, you know, an affective quality.
sentences.zh: 他们想到的是那些，你知道的，带有情感色彩的词汇。

sentences.en: But what you're really finding is that it's almost the connective tissue between words
sentences.zh: 但你真正发现的是，几乎是词汇之间的连接组织，

sentences.en: that actually reveals the inner workings of our minds.
sentences.zh: 才真正揭示了我们内心世界的运作方式。

sentences.en: That's exactly the way I think about it, is these words, what I love about them is they're
sentences.zh: 我正是这样看待它的，这些词汇，我喜欢它们的地方在于它们是

sentences.en: We can't control them very well.
sentences.zh: 我们无法很好地控制它们。

sentences.en: But they are revealing parts of ourselves that we just didn't know that we were, you
sentences.zh: 但它们却在揭示我们自己都没意识到的部分，你知道，

sentences.en: know, that we were spilling those beans.
sentences.zh: 我们无意中泄露了这些秘密。

sentences.en: What is striking about these function words is how few there are and how often we use them.
sentences.zh: 这些功能词最引人注目的是它们的数量很少，而且我们使用它们的频率极高。

sentences.en: There are not that many in the English language.
sentences.zh: 在英语中，这类词并不多。

sentences.en: There are only about 200 common ones.
But we use these function words at very high rates.
sentences.zh: 但我们使用这些功能词的频率非常高。

sentences.en: For example, these pronouns, prepositions, and articles, etc.
sentences.zh: 例如，这些代词、介词和冠词等等，
约占我们所说、所听到的

sentences.en: all the words we say, we hear.
The majority of words you and I have spoken have been function words in this conversation,
sentences.zh: 在这场对话中，你我所说的大部分词汇都是功能词，

sentences.en: and we don't even know it.
sentences.zh: 而我们甚至都没有察觉到。

sentences.en: I confess I was skeptical about these conclusions.
sentences.zh: 我承认，我最初对这些结论持怀疑态度。

sentences.en: We can understand profound things about others and even ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我们可以从中理解关于他人甚至我们自己的深刻道理。

sentences.en: All of these function words together are so powerful because they are telling us about
sentences.zh: 所有这些功能词加在一起之所以如此强大，是因为它们告诉了我们

sentences.en: If we're looking inward, a lot of it is telling us where we're paying attention and how we're
sentences.zh: 如果我们向内审视，很大程度上它在告诉我们关注点在哪里，我们是如何

sentences.en: thinking and what our connections with others are.
sentences.zh: 思考的，以及我们与他人的联系是什么。

sentences.en: So one thing that I want to point out and flag is that the differences in the rate at which
sentences.zh: 所以我想指出并强调的一点是，这些词汇的使用频率差异

sentences.en: these words are used can be subtle.
So it's not as if you can listen to someone's conversation intuitively and pick up the fact
sentences.zh: 所以，你不能凭直觉听出某人的谈话，然后就察觉到

sentences.en: that they're using more of these kinds of function words or fewer of these function words.
sentences.zh: 他们使用了更多或更少这类功能词。

sentences.en: In some ways, these have to be analyzed almost at a statistical level.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，这些必须在统计学层面进行分析。

sentences.en: A good example is people who are depressed use I words at higher rate than when they're
